known_diffs.reason: debug_verbosity receives a string instead of the expected type. Both clients reject it with -32602 (Invalid params); only the wording differs (geth: Go unmarshal error; reth: serde error). The behavior is equivalent.

error.message: invalid argument 0: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type int

known_diffs.reason: debug_verbosity lacks a required parameter. Both clients return -32602; only the wording differs (geth: missing value; reth: No more params). The behavior is equivalent.

For a negative debug_verbosity level, geth accepts the int and returns null; reth expects a usize and rejects the negative value with -32602. This is a semantic difference that does not affect normal use.

With extra debug_verbosity parameters, geth strictly checks the count and returns -32602 ('too many arguments'); reth ignores the extra parameters and returns null using the first one. This is a semantic difference.

error.message: too many arguments, want at most 1

known_diffs.reason: debug_vmodule receives an integer instead of the expected type. Both clients return -32602; only the wording differs, so the behavior is equivalent.

error.message: invalid argument 0: json: cannot unmarshal number into Go value of type string

known_diffs.reason: debug_vmodule receives a named-level pattern (reth::rpc=debug). Reth's tracing EnvFilter accepts the level name and returns null; geth accepts only filename=N with a numeric level and returns -32000. The clients use different vmodule pattern syntax, so this difference is expected.

debug_printBlock returns a Go struct debug dump string (*types.Block(...)) on geth; reth does not implement the method and returns null. This is debug output rather than consensus data, so the semantic difference is acceptable.

eth_config returns a chain configuration object (including current/next forkId) on reth. Geth's RPC handler crashes and returns -32603 ('method handler crashed'), indicating that geth does not implement it correctly. This semantic difference is recorded pending a geth-side fix.

admin_nodeInfo has the same top-level keys (enode/enr/id/ip/listenAddr/name/ports/protocols) on both clients, but values naturally differ by node identity: geth reports name='Geth/...' and the snap protocol, while reth reports name='op-reth-rpc2' and only eth. These are expected differences in node self-description.

debug_setHead was tested with tools/rpc_sethead_test.py: geth actually rewinds the head from N to N-2 and returns null when setHead targets N-2; reth's no-op stub leaves the head unchanged and also returns null. The behavior differs substantially. After the geth follower rewinds, its op-node derivation stalls at 'failed to retrieve L2 parent block' and does not recover on its own; run `task restart -- op-node-rpc1` to restore it.

baseline_example._note: Head actually rewinds from N to N-2
